chunks: 5 - He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, he said: Hisham ibn Muhammad ibn al-Saib informed us, from Abu Mikhnaf Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Husairah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ubaid ibn al-Kanud, who said:

Amirul Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) arrived from Basra to Kufa on the twelfth night of Rajab. He proceeded until he ascended the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, then said: As for what follows, all praise be to God who helped His ally, forsook His enemy, honored the truthful and righteous, and disgraced the lying falsifier.

O people of this town, it is incumbent upon you to be mindful of God and to obey those from the Ahlulbayt of your Prophet (may God bless him and his family) who obey God, for they are more worthy of your obedience insofar as they obey God, rather than the pretenders, claimants, and opponents who turn against us, boasting of our merit while denying it, disputing our right and pushing us from it. They have tasted the evil consequences of what they committed, and soon they shall meet perdition. Indeed, some men among you held back from helping me, and I am displeased and disdainful of them. So shun them and let them hear what they dislike, until they mend their ways or we see from them what pleases us.

Then Malik ibn Habib al-Tamimi al-Yarbui, his police commander, stood up and said: By God, I consider shunning and admonishing them too little. By God, if you command us, we will kill them all. Amirul Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: O Malik, you have crossed the limit, transgressed the boundary, and gone to extremes. He said: O Amirul Mu'minin, sometimes a bit of tyranny is more effective in matters that confront you than making peace with the enemies. Amirul Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: That is not how God decreed, O Malik. God Most High said: 'A life for a life' (5:45). So what is the point of tyranny? And God, glorified be He, said: 'And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given power to his heir, but let him not exceed the just limits in killing. Indeed, he will be aided' (17:33).

Then Abu Burdah ibn Awf al-Azdi stood before him. He was a partisan of Uthman who had held back on the day of the Battle of the Camel but joined at Siffin with a weak intention. He said: O Amirul Mu'minin, did you see those slain around Aisha, Talha, and al-Zubair? Why were they killed? Amirul Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Because they killed my followers and my governors, and for killing the brother of Rabiah al-Abdi along with a group of Muslims who said: 'We will not break our allegiance as you broke yours, and we will not betray as you betrayed.' So they attacked them and killed them unjustly. I asked them to hand over the killers so I could execute them, and the Book of God would judge between us. But they refused and fought me while my allegiance was on their necks and the blood of nearly a thousand of my followers was on them. So I fought them for that. Are you in doubt about that? He said: I was in doubt, but now I have understood, and the error of those people has become clear to me. Indeed, you are the rightly guided and the correct one.

Then Ali (peace be upon him) prepared to descend, and some men rose to speak, but when they saw him descend, they sat down and did not speak. Abu al-Kanud said: Despite his presence at Siffin, Abu Burdah was being hypocritical toward Amirul Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and used to write secretly to Muawiya. When Muawiya prevailed, he granted him a piece of land in al-Fallujah and was generous toward him.

key_terms.البيعة: Oath of allegiance, the pledge of loyalty
key_terms.المبطل: The falsifier, one who promotes falsehood
key_terms.المنتحلين: The pretenders, those who falsely claim authority
key_terms.النفس بالنفس: A life for a life (Quran 5:45), principle of proportional retribution

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about justice and proportional retribution after the Battle of Jamal?
ai.summary: This narration records Imam Ali's (AS) sermon upon arriving in Kufa after the Battle of Jamal (36 AH). Addressing the Kufans, he praised God for His support, exhorted obedience to the Ahlulbayt, and rebuked those who withheld their support. When his police chief Malik ibn Habib proposed killing the dissenters, Ali firmly rejected extrajudicial violence by citing Quran 5:45 and 17:33, insisting on proportional justice. Abu Burdah ibn Awf then questioned why those killed in the Battle of Jamal deserved their fate, and Ali justified the battle by citing the murder of his followers and their refusal to submit the perpetrators to justice. The narrator concludes by noting that Abu Burdah was actually a secret correspondent of Muawiya.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Hammad, who reported from Muhammad ibn Sahl, who reported from Hisham ibn Muhammad ibn al-Saib, from Abu Mikhnaf Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Husairah, from Abdul Rahman Ibn Ubaid ibn al-Kanud, who said:

Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, (a.s.), returned from Basrah to al-Kufah on 12th Rajab and proceeded to climb the pulpit. He expressed his gratitude and praise to Allah and said: "All praise be to Allah Who has helped His servant, blessed with authority and forsaken His enemy. He exalted the truthful and just and disgraced the liar and unjust.

O people of the town, it is obligatory upon you to be mindful of your duties to Allah and to obey those who, from among the Ahlul Bayt of your Prophet, are obedient to Allah. They are worthier of your submission; for they, in submission to Allah, stood firm against the pretentious and our opponents who despite their dependence upon us for their guidance, fight against us, usurp our rights and deprive us...They have tasted the evil of their action and there awaits them a painful chastisement. Indeed, some of you have held themselves back from helping me and I am indeed, displeased and disappointed with them. So, you disassociate yourselves from them and admonish them, so that, they may realize their misconduct or come to do what we approve."

Then Malik ibn Habib al-Tamimi al-Yarbu'i, his police commander, stood up and said: "By Allah, I believe that simply disassociating and admonition is two little. By Allah, should you command us, we would kill them all." Amirul Mu’minin, (a.s.), said: "O Malik, you are crossing the bounds and transgressing the limit, engaging yourself in the extremes." He said: "O Amirul Mu’minin! Sometimes a little bit of tyranny and inequity, while dealing with the matters confronting you, is more suited than being kind to your enemies." Amirul Mu’minin, (a.s.) said: "O Malik, that is not the way Allah has ordained. He Most High, has said: ’A life for a life’ (al-Maidah, 5:45). So where is the room for a bit of inequity and tyranny? And then Allah, Most High, has said: ’And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given power to his avenger of blood, but let him not exceed the just limits in killing. Surely, he will be victorious’(Al-Israa’, 17:33)."

Then Abu Burdah ibn Awf al-Azdi stood before him. He was a partisan of Uthman, having fought against ‘Ali in the battle of Jamal, but joined him in Siffin with a very weak intention of helping. He said: "O Amirul Mu’minin! Did you see the fallen bodies around Aisha, Talha and al-Zubair? Why were they killed?" Amirul Mu’minin, (a.s.) said: "Because they had killed my followers and my appointed governors. And (also) because they killed the brother of Rabi'ah al-Abdi - may Allah bless him with mercy, together with a group of Muslims. They had said: ’We will not break our allegiance the way you did and we will not revolt the way you have revolted.’ So, they were unjustly attacked and killed. I asked them to submit to me, the names of those who killed my brethren and there would be the Book of Allah, to decide between me and them. They refused (to give me the names) and (instead) they rose to fight me, while they were still in allegiance to me, and the responsibility of having killed, nearly a thousand of my partisans lay upon their shoulders. That is why I killed them. Do you have any doubt about that?" He said: "I had a doubt but now I have understood and the error of those people has now become evident for me. No doubt, you are the rightly guided one."

Then ‘Ali, (a.s.) prepared to climb down, while some people rose to speak. But when they saw him climb down, they sat down and did not utter a word. Then Abul Kanud said: "In spite of his presence (with ‘Ali) at Siffin, Abu Burdah was insincere to ‘Ali, (a.s.) and used to privately correspond with Mu’awiyah. And when Mu’awiyah became the absolute monarch, he gave a piece of land to him at al-Fallujah and was quite generous to him."
